feed.title: Converters, Formatters & Checkers — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: generatedata
entry.summary: A tool generating realistic fake test data to a given schema (CSV, JSON, SQL). Unlike making data up by hand it produces fields like names and addresses consistently and in bulk.

entry.title: Google Safe Browsing
entry.summary: Checks whether a site is flagged as unsafe in Google’s Safe Browsing records.

entry.title: Invertexto
entry.summary: A site bundling small text utilities — reversing, counting, converting and more.

entry.title: JSCompress
entry.summary: A tool that minifies JavaScript in the browser to shrink its size.

entry.title: JSON Editor Online
entry.summary: A browser tool to inspect and edit JSON in tree and text views. Unlike a plain editor it folds and validates the structure, making large JSON easy to navigate.

entry.title: JSON Sort
entry.summary: A simple tool that alphabetically sorts and formats JSON keys.

entry.title: KeyCDN Tools
entry.summary: Bundles network tools like ping, traceroute, HTTP header and performance tests.

entry.title: Lorem Ipsum
entry.summary: The classic generator of placeholder text (lorem ipsum) for design mockups.

entry.title: Mockaroo
entry.summary: Generates realistic fake test data (CSV, JSON, SQL) to your chosen schema.

entry.title: Password Generator
entry.summary: A simple, security-focused password generator with adjustable length and character sets.

entry.title: Wappalyzer
entry.summary: Reveals which technologies (framework, server, analytics) a website runs on.

entry.title: Website Grader
entry.summary: A free tool that grades a site on performance, SEO, mobile and security.

entry.title: XML Sitemaps
entry.summary: Crawls a site and builds the sitemap.xml file for search engines.

entry.title: Beautifier.io
entry.summary: Formats JavaScript, HTML and CSS and unpacks minified code. Against Prettier it needs no install and can open obfuscated output back up — which is what you want when inspecting someone else’s minified bundle.

entry.title: CodeBeautify
entry.summary: A collection of formatting, validation and conversion tools covering JSON, XML, YAML, SQL and Base64. Against IT Tools it is broader but heavier on ads — it is hard to find a conversion it lacks.

entry.title: Debuggex
entry.summary: A visual regex tester that draws the expression as a state diagram, covering JavaScript, Python and PCRE. Where regex101 lists tokens, this draws a flow chart, which reads better for nested groups.

entry.title: Diffchecker
entry.summary: A diff tool for text, images, PDFs and folders. Against the `diff` command it handles formatted and visual comparison — the command line will not tell you what changed between two PDF contracts.

entry.title: ExtendsClass
entry.summary: A collection of developer tools: a REST client, a SQLite browser, XML and JSON validators, regex testing. Against collections like IT Tools it runs the heavier things — a database browser and an API client — in the browser too.

entry.title: IEEE-754 Converter
entry.summary: A two-way converter between decimal and IEEE-754 floating point, with individual bits toggleable. Against a calculator it shows where the rounding error comes from — this is where the 0.1 + 0.2 question is actually answered.

entry.title: IT Tools
entry.summary: Eighty-odd developer utilities on one page: hashes, JWT decoding, cron expressions, UUIDs, colour conversion. Unlike the one-tool-per-site alternatives, everything runs in the browser and the whole thing self-hosts with Docker, so nothing leaves your machine.

entry.title: JSONLint
entry.summary: A JSON validator and formatter that tells you which line failed and why. Against an editor plugin it needs nothing installed, which is what you want when checking a malformed API response in a hurry.

entry.title: Regulex
entry.summary: Draws JavaScript regular expressions as railroad diagrams. Against Debuggex it runs entirely client-side and exports the diagram as SVG, which makes it useful for documentation.

entry.title: regex101
entry.summary: Explains an expression token by token, and its debugger shows exactly where a match breaks down. Unlike RegExr, you can switch between the PCRE, JavaScript, Python and Go flavours.

entry.title: CORS Tester
entry.summary: Tests an API’s CORS headers from the outside, telling you which header causes the vague CORS error in the browser console.

entry.title: Crontab Guru
entry.summary: Translates a cron expression into plain language as you type and shows the next run times, ending the guesswork over asterisks and slashes.

entry.title: explainshell
entry.summary: Paste a shell command and it maps every fragment to its entry in the man page. Against reading `man` it works backwards — you learn what the `-xzvf` in front of you means without scanning the manual.

entry.title: gitignore.io
entry.summary: Generates a `.gitignore` from your operating system, editor and language choices — the end of retyping the same lines on every project.

entry.title: JSON Crack
entry.summary: Draws JSON as a node graph rather than a tree, so nested structures are visible at a glance. Against a JSON formatter that graph view is the point — faster than counting indentation to work out the shape of a deep response.

entry.title: Kody Tools
entry.summary: A collection of developer converters, formatters and generators. Against compilations like IT Tools it keeps visual and textual tools together — colour, image and code utilities in one place.

entry.title: RegExr
entry.summary: A regex tester and an alternative to regex101, with a simpler interface and a community library of patterns.

entry.title: Solid Dev Tools
entry.summary: A collection of online debugging and network tools for developers and sysadmins.

entry.title: Textise
entry.summary: Strips a page to text only. Besides removing ads and layout noise, it roughly approximates what a screen reader sees.

entry.title: Transform
entry.summary: A collection of format converters — JSON to TypeScript types, HTML to JSX, SVG to a React component. It ends hunting a separate site for each.
